items.title: The name
items.text: Nothing we could find trades as FilmStruck. Of two U.S. registrations for the mark, both filed on April 1, 2016, the one covering streaming services was cancelled on September 29, 2023. The other, for entertainment services, is still registered to Turner Classic Movies, Inc., whose declaration of continued use was accepted on December 6, 2023. We do not know what use was claimed.[^38]

items.title: The website
items.text: filmstruck.com showed a closing notice in December 2018. When we requested it on October 8, 2026 it forwarded to tcm.com.[^39]

items.title: The Criterion Channel
items.text: Relaunched by Criterion alone on April 8, 2019, in the United States and Canada, at $10.99 a month or $99.99 a year, with lower prices for those who signed up before launch. Its website was live when we checked in October 2026; we did not confirm its current prices.[^34][^35][^36][^39]

items.title: The Warner Bros. classics
items.text: Went to HBO Max, which launched on May 27, 2020 at $14.99 a month with “a selection of classic films curated in partnership with TCM” and films licensed from Criterion.[^37]

items.title: The international services
items.text: FilmStruck Curzon in Britain and the French and Spanish services opened between February and June 2018 and ceased on the same day as the American one.[^11][^19]

items.title: The subscribers
items.text: The closing notice promised an email “with details about your account and the refund process as applicable.” Watchlists were not carried anywhere; one subscriber described his queue being wiped on the morning of November 30.[^19][^33]

items.title: The petition
items.text: “Keep FilmStruck Alive” was never closed. It showed 106,696 signatures on October 8, 2026, against a goal the page gave as 150,000.[^25]

items.title: The staff
items.text: Turner declined to say how many people worked on FilmStruck or how many were affected by the closure.[^19]

blocks.title: Who owned the name

nodes.what: Files two trademark applications for FILMSTRUCK on April 1 and announces the service on April 26.[^1][^38]

nodes.owner: Turner, with Warner Bros. Digital Networks
nodes.what: Warner Bros. becomes a partner in the service, adds its classics and closes Warner Archive’s streaming service into it.[^12]
Acquires Time Warner, and FilmStruck with it. Closes the service on November 29.[^15][^19]
nodes.price: About $81.0B for all of Time Warner

nodes.what: Lets one registration lapse and keeps the other. The service has not returned.[^38]
nodes.price: Not for sale as far as we know

blocks.source: AT&T Inc., Form 8-K, June 15, 2018[^15]; Variety[^12][^19]; USPTO status records.[^38] FilmStruck was closed by its owner and was never in bankruptcy. Our sources do not trace the corporate ownership of Turner Classic Movies, Inc. after 2020, so the last step names only the registrant shown by the USPTO.
